For the retrospective paper audit, each team-season receives one holistic 0-2 score per qualitative face. The coder evaluates the totality of documented case evidence rather than mechanically summing the prototype's three operational questions.
0 = Absent or harmful. 1 = Partial or mixed. 2 = Clear alignment.

The KIRIN prototype uses a separate forward-looking diagnostic instrument: three Yes/Partial/No questions per face, converted to a 0-10 diagnostic score. The prototype score is an application of the framework, not a direct reproduction of the historical 0-2 coding instrument. The two scores must not be treated as numerically interchangeable.
(1) A holistic score from 0 to 2. (2) Evidence supporting the score. (3) A short coding rationale. (4) The coder's identity. (5) Whether a second coder reviewed the case.

A score of 0 requires evidence that the factor was absent or materially harmful. A score of 1 requires mixed, incomplete, or ambiguous evidence. A score of 2 requires clear and substantial alignment supported by documented evidence.
If coders disagree, record the initial scores and resolve the disagreement using the predefined procedure documented in the Coding Rubric sheet. Do not change a score without updating the rationale.
